## tabula

```text
package tabula // import "github.com/0xJean/tabula"

Package tabula is a zero-dependency, descriptor-driven single-table SQL engine
for PostgreSQL. A row struct carries lightweight `db` tags; Define validates
the declaration once at package initialization, derives static parameterized
statements and column privilege needs, and records them in a Registry for
verification (PREPARE/EXPLAIN, schema checks, SQL snapshots).

Host applications inject their own scope type S (e.g. a tenant scope or
struct{}), value converters, and error classification via RegistryConfig so this
package stays decoupled from any application domain or error taxonomy.

CONSTANTS

const (
	// Write-guard and optimistic concurrency sentinel errors (used when
	// ErrorPolicy leaves the corresponding slot nil).
	ErrConflict           staticError = "row conflict or lost update"
	ErrOnce               staticError = "insert-only column changed on update"
	ErrNotDeleted         staticError = "soft delete needs the deleted column set"
	ErrRowCount           staticError = "write did not confirm exactly one row"
	ErrReadOnly           staticError = "operation requires a writable session and table"
	ErrScopeMismatch      staticError = "row scope differs from the bound session"
	ErrForbiddenStatement staticError = "statement attempts to modify session role or configuration"

	// PostgreSQL error-class sentinels returned by default error classification.
	ErrUnique                staticError = "unique constraint violation"
	ErrForeignKey            staticError = "foreign key constraint violation"
	ErrCheck                 staticError = "check constraint violation"
	ErrNotNull               staticError = "not-null constraint violation"
	ErrSerialization         staticError = "serialization failure"
	ErrDeadlock              staticError = "deadlock detected"
	ErrRLSDenied             staticError = "row-level security policy denied the operation"
	ErrInsufficientPrivilege staticError = "insufficient PostgreSQL privilege"
	ErrCanceled              staticError = "statement canceled"
)

FUNCTIONS

func GuardNoSessionEscape(query string) error
    GuardNoSessionEscape rejects SQL queries that attempt to switch PostgreSQL
    roles or mutate session configuration from application/adapter SQL:
    SET [LOCAL|SESSION] ROLE, RESET ROLE, RESET ALL, SESSION AUTHORIZATION, and
    set_config(...). Statement boundaries (;) are tracked so column assignments
    like "UPDATE users SET role = $2" are allowed while standalone or stacked
    "SET ROLE ..." / "SET role = ..." statements are rejected. Comments and
    single-quoted string literals are ignored to avoid false positives.

    Pass it directly to stdsql.ScopePolicy.GuardQuery or
    pgxdriver.ScopePolicy.GuardQuery.

func GuardReadOnly(query string) error
    GuardReadOnly admits a single SELECT or WITH statement and applies
    GuardNoSessionEscape. Adapters must also use a read-only PostgreSQL
    connection to enforce write restrictions inside CTEs and functions.

func IsCheckViolation(err error) bool
    IsCheckViolation reports PostgreSQL check_violation (SQLSTATE 23514).

func IsDeadlock(err error) bool
    IsDeadlock reports PostgreSQL deadlock_detected (SQLSTATE 40P01).

func IsForeignKeyViolation(err error) bool
    IsForeignKeyViolation reports PostgreSQL foreign_key_violation (SQLSTATE
    23503).

func IsNotNullViolation(err error) bool
    IsNotNullViolation reports PostgreSQL not_null_violation (SQLSTATE 23502).

func IsNumericOutOfRange(err error) bool
    IsNumericOutOfRange reports SQLSTATE 22003.

func IsQueryCanceled(err error) bool
    IsQueryCanceled reports PostgreSQL query_canceled (SQLSTATE 57014).

func IsRejectedValue(err error) bool
    IsRejectedValue reports a value refused by column definitions: string data
    right truncation (22001), numeric value out of range (22003), not_null
    violation (23502), check violation (23514), or invalid text representation
    (22P02).

func IsRetryable(err error) bool
    IsRetryable reports whether err is a PostgreSQL serialization failure
    (SQLSTATE 40001 / ErrSerialization) or deadlock (SQLSTATE 40P01 /
    ErrDeadlock).

func IsSerializationFailure(err error) bool
    IsSerializationFailure reports PostgreSQL serialization_failure (SQLSTATE
    40001).

func IsUniqueViolation(err error) bool
    IsUniqueViolation reports PostgreSQL unique_violation (SQLSTATE 23505).

func JSON(p any) any
    JSON addresses a json/jsonb column held as any Go value (text in and out).
    NULL reads as the zero value; a nil pointer value writes NULL.

func NewSessionGuard(cfg SessionGuardConfig) (func(string) error, error)
    NewSessionGuard compiles an application GuardQuery for trusted adapter SQL.
    RESET ALL and DISCARD ALL are rejected if they could reset protected state.

func RegisterType[S, V any](r *Registry[S], wrap func(*V) any)
    RegisterType registers a converter wrapping a pointer to a value of type T.
    Call during initialization before Define.

func RegisterZero[S, V any](r *Registry[S])
    RegisterZero registers scalar type V for the ",zero" db tag option (NULL
    scans as V's zero value; writes bind V directly).

func Retry(ctx context.Context, cfg RetryConfig, fn func(context.Context) error) error
    Retry invokes fn up to cfg.MaxAttempts times while fn returns a retryable
    error and ctx has not been canceled.

func SQLState(err error) string
    SQLState returns the five-character PostgreSQL SQLSTATE carried by err
    (compatible with both lib/pq and pgx errors implementing SQLState() string),
    or "" when err carries none.

func Zero[V any](p *V) any
    Zero addresses a nullable scalar column as a plain value of type V.


TYPES

type Assignment struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Assignment is an atomic update constructed by Add or SetNow.

func Add[N number](column string, delta N) Assignment
    Add adds a bound numeric value to a column in PostgreSQL.

func SetNow(column string) Assignment
    SetNow assigns PostgreSQL's transaction timestamp, now(), to a column.

type Column[T any] struct {
	Name string
	Addr func(*T) any

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Column is an escape-hatch column of a row type T (TableSpec.Columns): its
    name and the address of the value that holds it, for a column the db tags do
    not declare (a legacy conversion, a generated column, or an array wrapper).

func Col[T any](name string, addr func(*T) any) Column[T]
    Col declares an escape-hatch column. A field with a db tag cannot also be
    declared here: tag it db:"-" first.

func (c Column[T]) Once() Column[T]
    Once marks a column as written on insert only.

func (c Column[T]) Secret() Column[T]
    Secret marks a column's values as redacted in statement logs even when
    LogConfig.Values is ValuesAllowed.

type CountMode int
    CountMode controls how Rows.List obtains the total row count.

const (
	// CountExact runs SELECT count(*) with the active filter (default).
	CountExact CountMode = iota
	// CountNone skips the count query and returns -1 for total.
	CountNone
	// CountEstimate reads PostgreSQL's pg_class.reltuples estimate for the
	// table instead of scanning rows with COUNT(*).
	CountEstimate
)
type DefinedColumn struct {
	Name     string
	GoType   string
	Nullable bool
	Role     string
	Once     bool
	Secret   bool
}
    DefinedColumn is one column's metadata for schema and privilege checks.

type DefinedPrivilege struct {
	Table, Privilege string
	Columns          []string
	Sequence         string
	Function         string
}
    DefinedPrivilege is one privilege a defined table or view needs:
      - SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE on table columns
      - DELETE on a table
      - USAGE on a serial key's sequence
      - EXECUTE on a PostgreSQL function signature (e.g. "public.fn(uuid,
        text)")

type Definition struct {
	Name       string
	Columns    []DefinedColumn
	Statements map[string]string
	Privileges []DefinedPrivilege
}
    Definition is one defined table as Registry.Defined lists it.

type ErrorClass string
    ErrorClass is the fixed error classification string used in structured logs
    and error inspection.

const (
	ClassUnique                ErrorClass = "unique"
	ClassForeignKey            ErrorClass = "foreign_key"
	ClassCheck                 ErrorClass = "check"
	ClassNotNull               ErrorClass = "not_null"
	ClassSerialization         ErrorClass = "serialization"
	ClassDeadlock              ErrorClass = "deadlock"
	ClassCanceled              ErrorClass = "canceled"
	ClassRLSDenied             ErrorClass = "rls_denied"
	ClassInsufficientPrivilege ErrorClass = "insufficient_privilege"
	ClassOther                 ErrorClass = "other"
)
func ClassifyError(ctx context.Context, err error) (ErrorClass, error)
    ClassifyError inspects ctx and err (by context cancellation or PostgreSQL
    SQLSTATE) and returns its ErrorClass plus the matching tabula sentinel error
    (nil for ClassOther).

type ErrorPolicy struct {
	Classify    func(ctx context.Context, err error) error
	Sanitize    func(err error) string
	Conflict    error
	OnceChanged error
	NotDeleted  error
	RowCount    error
}
    ErrorPolicy maps execution and write-guard failures into the host's own
    error categories. Nil fields fall back to the package's default sentinels.

type Filter struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Filter accumulates optional predicates of one query over numbered bind
    parameters ($1..$n). Every value is bound; clause text is static adapter
    SQL.

    And replaces each single "?" of its clause, in order, with the next
    parameter. Write "??" to emit a literal "?" (for PostgreSQL JSONB operators
    such as ?, ?|, ?&). A marker/value mismatch is not repaired so malformed
    clauses fail loudly at prepare or execution.

func NewFilter(fixed ...any) *Filter
    NewFilter starts a filter whose fixed values occupy $1..$n.

func (f *Filter) And(clause string, values ...any)
    And appends one predicate; it is parenthesized when joined.

func (f *Filter) AndIf(cond bool, clause string, values ...any)
    AndIf appends clause with values only when cond is true.

func (f *Filter) Arg(v any) string
    Arg binds one value and returns its placeholder.

func (f *Filter) Args() []any
    Args returns a copy of the bound values in placeholder order.

func (f *Filter) In(column string, values ...any)
    In appends "<column> IN ($n, $n+1, ...)" for values. When values is empty,
    it appends "FALSE" so an empty list safely matches zero rows without
    producing invalid SQL. column must be a static SQL identifier.

func (f *Filter) Joined() string
    Joined returns the predicates joined by " AND " without leading connector.

func (f *Filter) Page(limit, offset any) string
    Page binds limit and offset and returns " LIMIT $a OFFSET $b".

func (f *Filter) Range(column string, from, to any)
    Range appends inclusive lower/upper bounds on column, omitting whichever
    bound is nil (including typed nil pointers). column must be a static SQL
    identifier.

func (f *Filter) Where() string
    Where returns the predicates as " AND (p1) AND (p2)", or "" when none.

type JSONValue struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    JSONValue holds a pointer to any Go value of a json/jsonb column.

func (v *JSONValue) Scan(src any) error

func (v *JSONValue) Value() (driver.Value, error)

type KeysetListing struct {
	// SortColumn optionally specifies a primary sort column (must be declared
	// on the Table). When empty, pagination orders directly by the key columns.
	SortColumn string
	// Direction is "ASC" (default when empty) or "DESC".
	Direction string
	// After holds the cursor values from the last item of the previous page,
	// matching the keyset tuple order: (SortColumn, key...) or (key...) when
	// SortColumn is empty or already part of the key.
	After []any
	// Limit is the maximum number of items to return (must be > 0). The engine
	// fetches Limit+1 rows to determine HasMore accurately.
	Limit int
	// Lock selects the row-lock clause and remembers locked rows for once checks.
	Lock LockMode
}
    KeysetListing requests one cursor-paginated page ordered by (SortColumn,
    key columns) without OFFSET scan degradation.

type KeysetPage[T any] struct {
	Items   []T
	HasMore bool
}
    KeysetPage is one cursor-paginated slice plus whether another page exists.

type Listing struct {
	Order        string
	Size, Offset int
	Lock         LockMode
	Count        CountMode
}
    Listing is a List/Find page request: Order (table default when empty),
    Size/Offset (all rows when Size <= 0), Lock (a PostgreSQL row-lock mode),
    and Count (CountExact default, CountNone, or CountEstimate).

type LockMode uint8
    LockMode selects the PostgreSQL row-lock clause of a listing.

const (
	LockNone       LockMode = iota
	LockUpdate              // FOR UPDATE
	LockSkipLocked          // FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
	LockNoWait              // FOR UPDATE NOWAIT
	LockShare               // FOR SHARE
)
type LogConfig struct {
	Logger        *slog.Logger
	Level         LogLevel
	LevelVar      *LogLevelVar
	SlowThreshold time.Duration
	Values        LogValues
	// Sample applies to LogAll only (0 < Sample < 1 samples that fraction;
	// 0 or >= 1 logs all statements). Errors and slow statements are never sampled.
	Sample float64
	// SQL includes the statement SQL as "tabula.sql" when Level is LogAll.
	SQL bool
	// Now supplies the clock for statement duration, defaulting to time.Now.
	// Active logging or a Metrics hook enables timing.
	Now func() time.Time
}
    LogConfig configures opt-in structured logging via log/slog on a Registry.
    Logging requires a registry or binding logger and a level other than LogOff.

type LogLevel int32
    LogLevel controls which statement executions are emitted to the configured
    slog.Logger.

const (
	// LogOff disables statement logging completely (default).
	LogOff LogLevel = iota
	// LogErrors logs failed statements only.
	LogErrors
	// LogSlow logs failed statements and statements slower than SlowThreshold.
	LogSlow
	// LogAll logs every statement (for debugging; not for production traffic).
	LogAll
)
type LogLevelVar struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    LogLevelVar is an atomic runtime switch for LogLevel that can be shared
    across one or more registries or adjusted without restarting.

func NewLogLevelVar(level LogLevel) *LogLevelVar
    NewLogLevelVar creates a LogLevelVar initialized to level.

func (l *LogLevelVar) Level() LogLevel
    Level returns the current LogLevel.

func (l *LogLevelVar) Set(level LogLevel)
    Set atomically updates the active LogLevel.

type LogValues int
    LogValues controls whether bound argument values appear in statement logs.

const (
	// ValuesNever omits all bound argument values from log output (default).
	ValuesNever LogValues = iota
	// ValuesRedacted logs only each argument's Go type and length.
	ValuesRedacted
	// ValuesAllowed logs bound argument values except secret columns and
	// statements marked with Secret(), which are always replaced by "[redacted]".
	ValuesAllowed
)
type Metrics interface {
	Observe(ctx context.Context, info TraceInfo, duration time.Duration, rows int64, errClass ErrorClass)
}
    Metrics observes latency, row count, and error class for each statement
    execution. Passed explicitly via RegistryConfig.Metrics; nil disables
    metrics.

type OrderSpec struct {
	Columns          map[string]string
	DefaultColumn    string
	DefaultDirection string
	TieBreaker       string
}
    OrderSpec resolves caller-supplied sort field and direction against a fixed
    whitelist and returns a safe SQL ORDER BY expression for Listing.Order.

func MustOrderSpec(spec OrderSpec) OrderSpec
    MustOrderSpec validates spec and returns an immutable copy. Any malformed
    specification panics at package initialization.

func (s OrderSpec) Resolve(by, dir string) string
    Resolve maps caller-provided sort key and direction to a safe SQL ORDER BY
    expression (without leading "ORDER BY").

type Registry[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Registry owns registered value converters, error policy, logging, tracing,
    metrics, and the list of defined tables and views. Applications normally
    declare one package-level Registry and may construct isolated registries in
    tests.

func NewRegistry[S any](cfg RegistryConfig[S]) *Registry[S]
    NewRegistry creates a Registry preloaded with built-in scalar zero
    converters (string, bool, int, int32, int64, float64, time.Time).

func (r *Registry[S]) Defined() []Definition
    Defined lists every table defined in r in definition order. The returned
    definitions are deep copies.

func (r *Registry[S]) DefinedViews() []ViewDefinition
    DefinedViews returns snapshots of all registered views in definition order.

func (r *Registry[S]) LogLevel() LogLevel
    LogLevel returns this Registry's active statement logging level.

func (r *Registry[S]) Resolve(ft reflect.Type, jsonOption, zeroOption bool) (func(any) any, error)
    Resolve returns the converter of a pointer to a value of type ft in r:
     1. json option: json text in and out;
     2. zero option: registered scalar, NULL read as the zero value;
     3. registry types (registered via RegisterType / ScopeWrap);
     4. types whose pointer implements sql.Scanner and driver.Valuer;
     5. database/sql native primitives (bool, ints, floats, string, []byte,
        time.Time).

func (r *Registry[S]) SetLogLevel(level LogLevel)
    SetLogLevel atomically updates this Registry's statement logging level.

type RegistryConfig[S any] struct {
	// Prefix labels panic and declaration error messages (defaults to "tabula").
	Prefix string
	// ScopeID extracts the raw SQL bind argument from a scope value S.
	// When omitted, the scope value itself identifies the row scope.
	ScopeID func(S) any
	// ScopeWrap wraps a *S pointer into a sql.Scanner / driver.Valuer.
	// Optional when S already implements sql.Scanner and driver.Valuer.
	ScopeWrap func(*S) any
	// ScopeLog formats a scope value S into the "tabula.scope" log attribute.
	// When nil, "tabula.scope" is omitted from log entries.
	ScopeLog func(S) string
	// ArrayArg wraps a Go slice for PostgreSQL "= ANY($n)" parameters
	// (e.g. pqdriver.Array). When nil, slices are passed as-is (native pgx).
	ArrayArg func(any) any
	// ArrayColumn resolves a db:"...,array" column's Go slice type into a
	// converter (e.g. pqdriver.ArrayColumn).
	ArrayColumn func(reflect.Type) (func(any) any, error)
	// Errors maps driver and write-guard failures for Rows created from this
	// registry.
	Errors ErrorPolicy
	// Log configures opt-in structured statement logging via log/slog.
	Log LogConfig
	// Tracer optionally wraps every statement execution in a tracing span.
	Tracer Tracer
	// Metrics optionally records latency, row count, and error class per statement.
	Metrics Metrics
}
    RegistryConfig configures one isolated Registry for scope type S.

type RetryConfig struct {
	// MaxAttempts is the total number of attempts including the initial run
	// (defaults to 3 when <= 0).
	MaxAttempts int
	// BaseDelay is the initial exponential backoff delay (defaults to 25ms when <= 0).
	BaseDelay time.Duration
	// MaxDelay caps the backoff delay (defaults to 500ms when <= 0).
	MaxDelay time.Duration
	// ShouldRetry overrides retry eligibility (defaults to IsRetryable).
	ShouldRetry func(error) bool
	// Sleep overrides the delay wait (useful for deterministic unit tests).
	Sleep func(context.Context, time.Duration) error
}
    RetryConfig controls explicit retries for transient PostgreSQL transaction
    conflicts (serialization failure 40001 and deadlock 40P01).

type Rows[T, K, S any] struct {
	readBinding[T, S]

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Rows is a Table bound to one Session. Bind it once per transaction: it
    remembers the once columns of rows it locked, and Save / UpdateWhere refuse
    a locked row whose once columns changed.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Args(row T) []any
    Args returns bound values matching Table.Insert().

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) CheckWrite(row *T) error
    CheckWrite validates the table mode and row scope for a write. Driver
    adapters use it when sending rows through a bulk protocol such as COPY.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Delete(ctx context.Context, key K) error
    Delete physically deletes the row identified by key within the session
    scope. Requires TableSpec.AllowDelete = true. Returns the conflict error
    when zero rows matched (missing or already deleted).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) DeleteWhere(ctx context.Context, where string, values ...any) (int64, error)
    DeleteWhere physically deletes rows matching the session scope and a
    required non-empty static predicate over "?" placeholders. Requires
    TableSpec.AllowDelete = true. Returns the affected row count; zero rows
    matched is not an error.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Exec(ctx context.Context, want int64, query string, args ...any) error
    Exec runs a hand-written write and confirms its row count (when want >= 0).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) ExistsBy(ctx context.Context, where string, values ...any) (bool, error)
    ExistsBy reports whether any undeleted row in the session's row scope
    matches where (a static predicate over bound "?" markers).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Find(ctx context.Context, where func(*Filter), l Listing) ([]T, error)
    Find reads undeleted rows matching where without running COUNT(*).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Get(ctx context.Context, key K) (*T, error)
    Get reads the undeleted row key without a lock; nil when missing.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) GetBy(ctx context.Context, where string, values ...any) (*T, error)
    GetBy reads the first undeleted row (in Order) matching where; nil when
    missing. where is a static predicate over bound "?" markers.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) GetMany(ctx context.Context, keys []K) ([]T, error)
    GetMany reads all undeleted rows whose key is in keys within the session
    scope. An empty keys slice returns nil, nil without issuing SQL.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Insert(ctx context.Context, row *T) error
    Insert writes row; with a serial key the generated key is read back into
    row.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) InsertMany(ctx context.Context, rows []T) error
    InsertMany inserts all rows using multi-row INSERT ... VALUES (...), (...).
    An empty slice returns nil without issuing SQL. Large batches are chunked
    automatically to stay within PostgreSQL's 65,535 bind parameter limit.
    All rows in a scoped call must share the session's scope.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) InsertReturning(ctx context.Context, row *T, columns ...string) error
    InsertReturning writes row and scans the named columns (or all table columns
    when columns is empty) back into row via RETURNING.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Iter(ctx context.Context, where func(*Filter), l Listing) iter.Seq2[T, error]
    Iter streams a Find query, applying the same scope, ordering, paging
    and lock mode. Breaking the range closes the cursor. Locked rows retain
    once-column snapshots.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) List(ctx context.Context, where func(*Filter), l Listing) ([]T, int64, error)
    List reads undeleted rows matching where for the listing plus total
    count according to l.Count (CountExact default, CountNone returns -1,
    CountEstimate reads PostgreSQL pg_class.reltuples).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) ListKeyset(ctx context.Context, where func(*Filter), l KeysetListing) (KeysetPage[T], error)
    ListKeyset reads one cursor-paginated page of undeleted rows matching where
    in deterministic (SortColumn, key...) order without OFFSET.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Lock(ctx context.Context, key K) (*T, error)
    Lock reads the undeleted row key FOR UPDATE; nil when missing.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) LockBy(ctx context.Context, where string, values ...any) (*T, error)
    LockBy reads and locks (FOR UPDATE) the first undeleted row (in Order)
    matching where; nil when missing. The row's once columns are remembered.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) LockMany(ctx context.Context, keys []K) ([]T, error)
    LockMany reads and locks (FOR UPDATE) all undeleted rows whose key is
    in keys in deterministic ascending key order to avoid deadlocks across
    concurrent transactions. Once columns of every locked row are remembered.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Save(ctx context.Context, row T) error
    Save writes every updatable column of the undeleted row at the previous
    version (when versioned); no row updated returns the conflict error.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) SaveReturning(ctx context.Context, row *T, columns ...string) error
    SaveReturning writes every updatable column of the undeleted row (honoring
    optimistic version CAS and once-column protection) and scans the named
    columns (or all columns when empty) back into row via RETURNING. No row
    matched returns the conflict error.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Scan(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Scan runs a hand-written single-row SELECT.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Scope() *Filter
    Scope starts a Filter seeded with the session scope predicate (none on an
    unscoped session) and soft-delete predicate.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Select(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) ([]T, error)
    Select scans every row of a hand-written SELECT over Table.Cols().

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) SelectIter(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) iter.Seq2[T, error]
    SelectIter streams a hand-written SELECT over Table.Cols().

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Set(ctx context.Context, row T, columns ...string) error
    Set writes only the named columns of the undeleted row (no version check).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) SetExpr(ctx context.Context, key K, assignments ...Assignment) error
    SetExpr applies assignments to one live row by key within the session scope.
    Like Set, it checks the affected row count and does not perform version CAS.
    Key, scope, deleted, version and once columns cannot be expression targets.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) SetWhere(ctx context.Context, row T, columns []string, where string, values ...any) (bool, error)
    SetWhere writes only the named columns of the undeleted row matching key
    (and scope when declared) plus an extra static SQL predicate over "?"
    placeholders. Reports whether a row matched; zero rows is not an error.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) SoftDelete(ctx context.Context, row T) error
    SoftDelete is a Save of a row whose deleted column is marked deleted
    (non-nil *time.Time, true bool, or configured DeletedValue).

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) UpdateWhere(ctx context.Context, row T, where string, values ...any) (bool, error)
    UpdateWhere writes every updatable column of the undeleted row matching key
    (and scope/version when declared) plus an extra static SQL predicate over
    "?" placeholders. Reports whether a row matched; zero rows is not an error.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) Upsert(ctx context.Context, plan *UpsertPlan[T, K, S], row *T) (bool, error)
    Upsert executes a pre-declared UpsertPlan for row. Returns (true, nil) when
    a row was inserted or updated, and (false, nil) when DO NOTHING or a DO
    UPDATE WHERE guard skipped the write. Any Returning columns are scanned into
    row.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) UpsertMany(ctx context.Context, plan *UpsertPlan[T, K, S], rows []T) (int64, error)
    UpsertMany returns the number of inserted or updated rows, excluding
    conflicts skipped by DO NOTHING or WHERE. The batch only returns a count:
    it omits the plan's RETURNING list and leaves the input slice untouched.
    On error the count covers successful chunks in the current transaction.

func (r *Rows[T, K, S]) WithLogger(logger *slog.Logger) *Rows[T, K, S]
    WithLogger returns a Rows handle sharing the same Table and Session with a
    per-binding logger override.

type Session[S any] interface {
	Scope() S
	Unscoped() bool
	Exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (int64, error)
	Scan(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
	Returning(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
	Each(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, decode func(func(...any) error) error) error
}
    Session executes SQL under a single fixed scope. Transaction adapters
    and Direct pools implement this interface. Each must close its cursor
    and stop on the first callback error. A session may implement ReadOnly()
    bool to decline derived writes and locking reads before any SQL is sent.
    S is the host application's row-scope value (for example a tenant, org,
    or workspace ID, or struct{} for applications without row-level scoping).

type SessionGuardConfig struct {
	VariablePrefixes           []string
	ForbidRole                 bool
	ForbidSessionAuthorization bool
	ForbidSetConfig            bool
}
    SessionGuardConfig selects prohibited session operations. Prefixes name GUC
    namespaces (for example "scope."). The constructor copies and folds them.
    Dynamic set_config keys are rejected whenever a namespace is protected.

type SoftDelete struct {
	// DeletedValue is the sentinel value written to mark a row deleted
	// (must be string/~string or an integer matching the ",deleted" field type).
	DeletedValue any
	// AliveValue, when non-nil, sets the live-row predicate to "<col> = <AliveValue>".
	// When nil, the live-row predicate is "<col> <> <DeletedValue>".
	AliveValue any
}
    SoftDelete configures status-value soft deletion on a ",deleted" column.
    Leave TableSpec.SoftDelete nil for *time.Time (deleted_at IS NULL) or bool
    (is_deleted = FALSE).

type StatementOption func(*stmtMeta)
    StatementOption configures per-statement logging behavior at registration
    time.

func Quiet() StatementOption
    Quiet suppresses non-error logging for a registered statement (never logged
    under LogSlow or LogAll; errors are still logged).

func Secret() StatementOption
    Secret forces every bound argument of a registered statement to be redacted
    as "[redacted]" even when LogConfig.Values is ValuesAllowed.

type Table[T, K, S any] struct {
	descriptor[T, S]

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Table is the compiled handle for a TableSpec. Its column bindings, SQL and
    access modes are fixed by Define.

func Define[T, K, S any](r *Registry[S], spec TableSpec[T, K]) *Table[T, K, S]
    Define validates spec against r (panicking on declaration mistakes at
    package initialization), derives its statements and column privileges,
    and records it in r.

func TryDefine[T, K, S any](r *Registry[S], spec TableSpec[T, K]) (*Table[T, K, S], error)
    TryDefine validates spec and returns a compiled table without registering
    it.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) AllowsDelete() bool
    AllowsDelete reports whether the table permits physical deletes.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) Bind(s Session[S]) *Rows[T, K, S]
    Bind binds the table to a transaction session.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) Cols() string
    Cols is the select list, for hand-written statements scanned with
    Rows.Select.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) DefineUpsert(key string, spec UpsertSpec, opts ...StatementOption) *UpsertPlan[T, K, S]
    DefineUpsert validates spec against t, registers its SQL statement under key
    in the Registry (so sqlcheck verifies it), and returns an executable plan.
    Panics on declaration errors at package initialization.

func (d *Table) Definition() Definition
    Definition returns a deep copy of the current registry entry.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) Insert() string
    Insert is the INSERT base without RETURNING, for hand-written variants.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) InsertColumns() []string
    InsertColumns returns the column names included in Table.Insert() in bind
    order.

func (d *Table) Name() string
    Name returns the name supplied at definition time.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) ReadOnly() bool
    ReadOnly reports whether the declaration permits only reads.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) Requires(table, privilege string, columns ...string) *Table[T, K, S]
    Requires registers an additional privilege required by this descriptor.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) RequiresFunction(signature string) *Table[T, K, S]
    RequiresFunction registers an additional privilege required by this
    descriptor.

func (d *Table) Statement(key, query string, opts ...StatementOption) string
    Statement registers hand-written SQL for verification and observation.
    Keys are unique within a table or view.

func (t *Table[T, K, S]) TryDefineUpsert(key string, spec UpsertSpec, opts ...StatementOption) (*UpsertPlan[T, K, S], error)
    TryDefineUpsert validates spec and builds an UpsertPlan without recording it
    in the Registry.

type TableSpec[T, K any] struct {
	Name, Order string
	Columns     []Column[T]
	SoftDelete  *SoftDelete
	// ReadOnly restricts this table to read operations only: no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
	// statements or write privileges are derived, and write methods return ErrReadOnly.
	ReadOnly bool
	// AllowDelete opts this table into physical DELETE statements (Delete / DeleteWhere)
	// and derives the table-level DELETE privilege for sqlcheck. Cannot combine with ReadOnly.
	AllowDelete bool
}
    TableSpec declares one table of rows T keyed by K: the qualified name,
    the default order of List, optional SoftDelete config, and the row type's
    db tags, read once by Define. Tag options: key, serial, scope, deleted,
    version, once, json, zero, array, secret.

type TraceInfo struct {
	Key    string
	Table  string
	Action string
	Scope  string
}
    TraceInfo identifies one statement execution for Tracer and Metrics hooks.
    Statement keys double as span names and metric labels.

type Tracer interface {
	Start(ctx context.Context, info TraceInfo) (context.Context, func(rows int64, err error))
}
    Tracer starts and ends a span around each statement execution. Passed
    explicitly via RegistryConfig.Tracer; nil disables tracing.

type UpsertPlan[T, K, S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    UpsertPlan is a validated, registered upsert statement bound to one Table.

func (u *UpsertPlan[T, K, S]) Key() string
    Key returns the registered statement key.

func (u *UpsertPlan[T, K, S]) SQL() string
    SQL returns the derived INSERT ... ON CONFLICT statement.

type UpsertSpec struct {
	Conflict  []string
	Update    []string
	Where     string
	Returning []string
}
    UpsertSpec declares a controlled PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
    statement. Conflict columns identify the unique index or constraint target.
    Update lists the columns updated on conflict (key, scope, and once columns
    are forbidden); leaving Update empty produces ON CONFLICT (...) DO NOTHING.

type View[T, S any] struct {
	descriptor[T, S]
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    View is the compiled row shape for a hand-written query.

func DefineView[T, S any](r *Registry[S], spec ViewSpec[T]) *View[T, S]
    DefineView validates v against r (panicking on declaration mistakes at
    package initialization) and records it in r.DefinedViews().

func TryDefineView[T, S any](r *Registry[S], spec ViewSpec[T]) (*View[T, S], error)
    TryDefineView validates v without recording it in r.

func (v *View[T, S]) Bind(s Session[S]) *ViewRows[T, S]
    Bind binds this projection to the scope of s.

func (v *View[T, S]) Cols() string
    Cols returns the comma-separated select column list in struct field order.

func (v *View[T, S]) ColsAs(alias string) string
    ColsAs returns the select column list qualified with table alias (e.g.
    "c.id, c.name").

func (v *View[T, S]) Definition() ViewDefinition
    Definition returns a deep copy of the registered view metadata.

func (d *View) Name() string
    Name returns the name supplied at definition time.

func (v *View[T, S]) Requires(table, privilege string, columns ...string) *View[T, S]
    Requires registers an additional privilege required by this descriptor.

func (v *View[T, S]) RequiresFunction(signature string) *View[T, S]
    RequiresFunction registers an additional privilege required by this
    descriptor.

func (v *View[T, S]) SelectAs(aliases map[string]string) string
    SelectAs generates a JOIN SELECT list from prefix-to-table-alias mappings
    (e.g. aliases{"o_": "o", "c_": "c"} produces "o.id AS o_id, ..., c.id AS
    c_id"). Columns whose prefix is not in aliases are emitted as their plain
    name.

func (d *View) Statement(key, query string, opts ...StatementOption) string
    Statement registers hand-written SQL for verification and observation.
    Keys are unique within a table or view.

type ViewDefinition Definition
    ViewDefinition describes a registered query projection.

type ViewRows[T, S any] struct{ readBinding[T, S] }
    ViewRows decodes hand-written SQL using the bound projection.

func (r *ViewRows[T, S]) Iter(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) iter.Seq2[T, error]
    Iter decodes rows as they arrive. Breaking the range releases the cursor.

func (r *ViewRows[T, S]) One(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (*T, error)
    One reads at most one row. A missing row returns nil, nil.

func (r *ViewRows[T, S]) Scan(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Scan executes a scalar single-row query with the registry error policy.

func (r *ViewRows[T, S]) Select(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) ([]T, error)
    Select decodes all rows of query.

func (r *ViewRows[T, S]) WithLogger(logger *slog.Logger) *ViewRows[T, S]
    WithLogger returns a handle with a per-binding logger override.

type ViewSpec[T any] struct {
	Name    string
	Columns []Column[T]
}
    ViewSpec declares a read-only row projection T (such as a JOIN result,
    summary, or auxiliary lookup table) without requiring a key, scope, deleted,
    or version column. It reuses the Registry's db-tag codecs (UUID, JSON, Zero,
    Array, custom Scanner/Valuer) and supports nested struct column prefixes
    (e.g. `Order OrderRow` tagged `db:"o_"` maps o_id, o_code, ...).

type ZeroValue[V any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ZeroValue holds a nullable column as a plain Go value: NULL reads as the
    zero value and the value is bound as itself.

func (v *ZeroValue[V]) Scan(src any) error

func (v *ZeroValue[V]) Value() (driver.Value, error)
```

## pgxdriver

```text
package pgxdriver // import "github.com/0xJean/tabula/pgxdriver"

Package pgxdriver integrates github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 with tabula: PostgreSQL
array column converters, transaction-bound Sessions, and pgxpool Runners with
pluggable scope/RLS policies and savepoints.

FUNCTIONS

func ArrayColumn(ft reflect.Type) (func(any) any, error)
    ArrayColumn selects pgx's native one-dimensional array codec. Its type map
    handles both built-in and named Go slices and element types.

func CopyFrom[T, K, S any](ctx context.Context, sess *Session[S], tbl *tabula.Table[T, K, S], rows []T) (int64, error)
    CopyFrom bulk-inserts rows into tbl using PostgreSQL's binary COPY protocol
    via pgx.Tx.CopyFrom. It uses the table's derived INSERT column list and
    value codecs (JSON, Zero, Array, custom Scanner/Valuer) and skips serial key
    and timestamp soft-delete columns automatically, matching Rows.Insert.

    An empty rows slice returns 0, nil without touching the database.

func SetLocalConfig(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, key, value string) error
    SetLocalConfig sets a PostgreSQL transaction-local GUC via set_config(...,
    true).

func SetLocalRole(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, role string) error
    SetLocalRole switches the PostgreSQL role for the duration of tx.


TYPES

type DirectOption func(*pgxpool.Config)
    DirectOption customizes the pgxpool.Config used by Direct before the pool
    is created. Direct always enforces default_transaction_read_only=on after
    applying options.

type DirectPool[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    DirectPool owns a pool of read-only pgx connections.

func Direct[S any](ctx context.Context, dsn string, policy ScopePolicy[S], opts ...DirectOption) (*DirectPool[S], error)
    Direct opens a dedicated pool with read-only mode in the startup parameters
    of every physical connection. Session binds each request without SQL.
    Transaction-local setup requires a Runner. Call Close at shutdown.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Close() error
    Close releases the underlying connection pool.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Session(scope S) tabula.Session[S]
    Session binds the scope without opening a transaction or checking out a
    connection.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Stat() *pgxpool.Stat
    Stat returns the current pgxpool statistics.

type Runner[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Runner opens scoped PostgreSQL transactions on a *pgxpool.Pool.

func NewRunner[S any](pool *pgxpool.Pool, policy ScopePolicy[S]) *Runner[S]
    NewRunner creates a Runner backed by pool and policy.

func (r *Runner[S]) Within(ctx context.Context, scope S, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    Within runs fn in a read-write transaction.

func (r *Runner[S]) WithinReadOnly(ctx context.Context, scope S, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    WithinReadOnly runs fn in a READ ONLY transaction.

func (r *Runner[S]) WithinTxOptions(ctx context.Context, scope S, opts pgx.TxOptions, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    WithinTxOptions runs fn inside a transaction opened with opts.

type ScopePolicy[S any] struct {
	SetupTx    func(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, scope S) error
	GuardQuery func(query string) error
	IsUnscoped func(scope S) bool
}
    ScopePolicy plugs application-specific isolation rules (scope GUC variables,
    SET LOCAL ROLE, or SQL guards) into a pgx Runner and its Sessions.

func NoScopePolicy() ScopePolicy[struct{}]
    NoScopePolicy returns an empty ScopePolicy for applications without
    row-level scoping.

type Session[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Session implements tabula.Session[S] over one pgx.Tx.

func NewSession[S any](tx pgx.Tx, scope S, policy ScopePolicy[S]) *Session[S]
    NewSession wraps an existing pgx.Tx with scope and policy.

func (s Session) Each(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, decode func(func(...any) error) error) error
    Each streams all rows of query through decode.

func (s *Session[S]) Exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (int64, error)
    Exec executes query and returns the affected row count.

func (s *Session[S]) ReadOnly() bool
    ReadOnly reports whether this session was opened as a READ ONLY transaction.

func (s *Session[S]) Returning(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Returning executes a write with RETURNING and maps pgx.ErrNoRows to
    sql.ErrNoRows.

func (s *Session[S]) Savepoint(ctx context.Context, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    Savepoint runs fn inside a nested pgx transaction (PostgreSQL SAVEPOINT).

func (s Session) Scan(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Scan executes a single-row query and maps pgx.ErrNoRows to sql.ErrNoRows.

func (s *Session[S]) Scope() S
    Scope returns the session's bound scope value.

func (s *Session[S]) Tx() pgx.Tx
    Tx returns the underlying pgx.Tx for low-level escape hatches.

func (s *Session[S]) Unscoped() bool
    Unscoped reports whether this session bypasses row-level scope predicates.
```

```text
package postgresfixture // import "github.com/0xJean/tabula/postgresfixture"

type Database struct {
```

## sqlcheck

```text
package sqlcheck // import "github.com/0xJean/tabula/sqlcheck"

Package sqlcheck verifies PostgreSQL descriptors, handwritten SQL and role
workloads. It checks schema alignment, snapshots database catalogs, compares
direct grants, trials revocations, classifies policies and tests RLS behavior.

FUNCTIONS

func CheckPolicyCoverage(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, work RoleStatements) ([]string, error)
    CheckPolicyCoverage reads pg_policy for each required command. It checks
    permissive rules, ALL/PUBLIC and inherited memberships, and flags bypassing
    roles on RLS tables. Predicates are exercised separately by RunRLSMatrix.

func CheckRLS(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, exp RLSExpectation) ([]string, error)
    CheckRLS audits PostgreSQL RLS configuration in exp.Schema against exp and
    returns sorted human-readable failure lines.

func CheckRolePrivileges(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, needs PrivilegeNeeds, role string) (missing, extra []string, err error)
    CheckRolePrivileges compares a PostgreSQL role's actual grants on db against
    needs, returning sorted missing and extra privilege descriptions.

func CheckSchemaColumns(def tabula.Definition, installed map[string]ColumnInfo, families map[string][]string) []string
    CheckSchemaColumns compares one descriptor Definition against the installed
    PostgreSQL columns for its table or view and returns human-readable mismatch
    lines.

func DefaultTypeFamilies() map[string][]string
    DefaultTypeFamilies returns a fresh copy of the built-in Go-type to
    PostgreSQL information_schema data_type family map. Callers may extend
    the returned map with application-specific named types before calling
    CheckSchemaColumns or VerifySchema.

func FirstDifference(want, got string) string
    FirstDifference returns up to 40 diff lines showing the first mismatches
    between want and got.

func ParseSnapshot(content string) ([]tabula.Definition, error)
    ParseSnapshot parses a SQL snapshot previously rendered by RenderSnapshot
    back into tabula.Definition entries (table name + named statements). This
    allows standalone CI tooling such as `tabula check` to verify a committed
    snapshot directly against PostgreSQL without importing the application's Go
    packages.

func PrepareStatement(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, query, role string) (err error)
    PrepareStatement has the server PREPARE query inside tx, optionally as role,
    then EXPLAIN EXECUTE it with NULL arguments. PREPARE checks names, types,
    functions and parameter inference. EXPLAIN checks plan-time access without
    executing the statement. Runtime function and sequence use needs execution
    probes. Row-level security policies are not evaluated. Everything is undone
    through a savepoint, so tx stays usable for the next statement.

func RenderAllSnapshot(tables []tabula.Definition, views []tabula.ViewDefinition, headerLines ...string) string
    RenderAllSnapshot renders both table Definitions and ViewDefinitions into
    one deterministic SQL snapshot.

func RenderSnapshot(defs []tabula.Definition, headerLines ...string) string
    RenderSnapshot formats every statement across defs deterministically (sorted
    by table name, then statement key), prefixed by headerLines (each written as
    a "-- " comment line).

func RunRLSMatrix(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, m RLSMatrix) ([]string, error)
    RunRLSMatrix executes application SQL against a disposable fixture and rolls
    back each cell independently. Findings are sorted. Transaction setup and
    rollback errors are returned separately from assertion failures.

func VerifyRoleStatements(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, work RoleStatements) ([]string, error)
    VerifyRoleStatements prepares and explains each role's SQL in a rolled-back
    transaction. Findings identify the role and statement and are sorted.

func VerifySchema(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, defs []tabula.Definition, families map[string][]string) ([]string, error)
    VerifySchema inspects PostgreSQL columns on db for every Definition in defs
    (supporting tables, partitioned tables, regular views, and materialized
    views) and returns all column mismatches.

func VerifyStatements(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, defs []tabula.Definition, role string) ([]string, error)
    VerifyStatements prepares and explains every statement of defs as role
    (empty means the connection's own role) inside one rolled-back transaction
    and returns one line per failing statement, sorted.

func VerifyViewSchema(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, views []tabula.ViewDefinition, families map[string][]string) ([]string, error)
    VerifyViewSchema verifies column alignment for views (including PostgreSQL
    regular views and materialized views) against db.

func VerifyViewStatements(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, views []tabula.ViewDefinition, role string) ([]string, error)
    VerifyViewStatements prepares and explains every registered statement across
    views as role inside one rolled-back transaction.

func ViewsToDefinitions(views []tabula.ViewDefinition) []tabula.Definition
    ViewsToDefinitions converts ViewDefinitions into Definitions so they
    can be passed to RenderSnapshot, VerifyStatements, VerifySchema,
    or CollectPrivilegeNeeds.


TYPES

type BehaviorCase struct {
	Role, Scope, Statement string
	Rows                   [][]*string
	Ordered                bool              `json:",omitempty"`
	Affected               *int64            `json:",omitempty"`
	Denied                 tabula.ErrorClass `json:",omitempty"`
}
    BehaviorCase expects exactly one outcome. Rows are PostgreSQL values scanned
    as text, with nil for SQL NULL. Unordered comparison preserves duplicates.

type BehaviorStatement struct {
	SQL  string
	Args []any
}
    BehaviorStatement executes once per role and scope, with bound arguments.

type Catalog struct {
	Policies []Policy
	ForceRLS []Relation
	Grants   []Grant
	Definers []Definer
}
    Catalog holds one repeatable-read snapshot. Policies, force flags and
    definers cover all objects in the selected schemas, regardless of grantee.

func ReadCatalog(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, scope CatalogScope) (Catalog, error)
    ReadCatalog reads the scoped PostgreSQL catalogs with a fixed deparser
    search path. It includes overloaded functions and explicit column grants.

func (c Catalog) Snapshots() map[string]string
    Snapshots renders each catalog section as independently comparable JSON.

type CatalogScope struct{ Schemas, Roles []string }
    CatalogScope names the complete set of schemas and direct grantees in an
    audit. PUBLIC includes privileges granted to everyone.

type ColumnInfo struct {
	DataType string
	Nullable bool
}
    ColumnInfo is one PostgreSQL column as read from information_schema.columns
    or pg_catalog.pg_attribute (for materialized views).

type Definer struct{ Schema, Name, Arguments, Owner, Definition string }
    Definer records the owner, signature, body and settings of a SECURITY
    DEFINER routine.

type Grant struct {
	Role, Schema, Kind, Object, Privilege string
	Column                                string `json:",omitempty"`
	Arguments                             string `json:",omitempty"`
	GrantOption                           bool   `json:",omitempty"`
}
    Grant is a direct ACL entry. Kind is TABLE, COLUMN, SEQUENCE or FUNCTION.
    Arguments uses schema-qualified PostgreSQL type names from the snapshot,
    including the array type name for variadic functions. Grantor is immaterial.

type GrantDiff struct {
	Missing, Extra []Grant
	SQL            []string
}
    GrantDiff contains both sides of the discrepancy and reviewable repair SQL.

func CheckGrantManifest(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, m GrantManifest) (GrantDiff, error)
    CheckGrantManifest compares a declaration against every supported object in
    its schemas.

func CompareGrants(manifest GrantManifest, actual []Grant) (GrantDiff, error)
    CompareGrants computes exact direct ACL differences, including grant
    options. PostgreSQL revokes same-privilege column ACLs when revoking from
    a table; surviving explicit column grants are restored in the generated
    script.

type GrantManifest struct {
	CatalogScope
	Grants []Grant
}
    GrantManifest declares the exact grants expected in its CatalogScope.

type InventoryConfig struct {
	Dir      string
	Patterns []string
	Tags     string
	// Tests includes internal and external _test.go files in matching packages.
	Tests      bool
	Methods    []SQLMethod
	Exceptions map[string]string
}
    InventoryConfig selects buildable Go packages and reviewed site exceptions.
    Patterns default to ./... in Dir. Tags use the Go build tag syntax.

type MinimizeConfig struct {
	Role       string
	Schemas    []string
	Statements []Statement
	Keep       []Grant
	// Current, if supplied, must match the live direct ACL exactly.
	Current []Grant
	// Runtime probes supplement planning for specified privileges.
	Runtime []RuntimeProbe
}
    MinimizeConfig selects one role and its complete planning workload. Keep
    pins runtime requirements, including requirements from outside the workload.

type Minimum struct {
	Kept, Removed, Unverified []Grant
	GrantSQL, RevokeSQL       []string
}
    Minimum records a deterministic, inclusion-minimal set for the tested
    DML privileges, plus pinned and unobservable privileges. Unverified lists
    surviving privileges for which planning alone is insufficient evidence.

func MinimizeGrants(ctx context.Context, db *sql.DB, cfg MinimizeConfig) (Minimum, error)
    MinimizeGrants tries cumulative RESTRICT revocations in an
    always-rolled-back transaction. It verifies the baseline, each candidate and
    the final workload. A trial that fails for a non-permission reason aborts
    the audit.

type Policy struct {
	PolicyID
	Command      string
	Permissive   bool
	Roles        []string
	Using, Check string
}
    Policy contains the server-deparsed conditions and explicit target roles.

type PolicyAccess struct{ Table, Command string }
    PolicyAccess names a relation (PostgreSQL regclass spelling) and a command
    requiring a permissive policy for the execution role.

type PolicyClass struct {
	PolicyID
	Rule string
}
    PolicyClass records the unique matching rule for a policy.

func ClassifyPolicies(policies []Policy, rules []PolicyRule) ([]PolicyClass, []string, error)
    ClassifyPolicies requires exactly one rule per policy and reports every
    registered identity that no longer satisfies its rule. It has no built-in
    roles.

type PolicyID struct {
	Relation
	Name string
}
    PolicyID identifies a policy within its table.

type PolicyRule struct {
	Name, Command, Using, Check string
	Permissive                  *bool
	Roles                       []string
	Entries                     []PolicyID
	// Patterns match individual identifiers. UnregisteredOnly excludes policy
	// identities explicitly registered in any rule's Entries.
	SchemaPattern, TablePattern, NamePattern string
	UnregisteredOnly                         bool
}
    PolicyRule matches the conjunction of its nonempty fields. Roles is an exact
    set; Using and Check are Go regular expressions over server-deparsed SQL.
    Entries, when present, restricts the rule to registered policy identities.

type PrivilegeNeeds struct {
	Columns     map[string]map[string]map[string]bool
	TableDelete map[string]bool
	Sequences   [][2]string
	Functions   []string
}
    PrivilegeNeeds aggregates column, table-DELETE, sequence, and function
    EXECUTE privileges required across a set of descriptor Definitions.

func CollectPrivilegeNeeds(defs []tabula.Definition) (PrivilegeNeeds, []string)
    CollectPrivilegeNeeds merges the Privileges declared on defs and also
    reports any definition names that declared zero privileges.

type RLSExpectation struct {
	// Schema is the PostgreSQL schema to inspect (defaults to "public").
	Schema string
	// Tables lists unqualified table names in Schema that must have RLS enabled.
	// When empty, every table in Schema that already has RLS enabled is audited.
	Tables []string
	// RequireForce fails any checked table without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
	RequireForce bool
	// RequireRestrictive fails any checked table that has no RESTRICTIVE policy.
	RequireRestrictive bool
	// ForbiddenPolicyRoles fails any policy in Schema whose polroles directly
	// names one of these roles (e.g. a login or grant-holder role).
	ForbiddenPolicyRoles []string
}
    RLSExpectation configures domain-agnostic PostgreSQL Row-Level Security
    structural checks against pg_class and pg_policy.

type RLSMatrix struct {
	Roles      []string
	Scopes     map[string]map[string]string
	Statements map[string]BehaviorStatement
	Cases      []BehaviorCase
}
    RLSMatrix requires one expectation for every role × scope × statement cell.
    Scopes contain application-owned custom GUC values.

type Relation struct{ Schema, Table string }
    Relation identifies one schema-qualified PostgreSQL relation.

type RoleStatements map[string][]Statement
    RoleStatements maps each execution role to its own named probes.

type RuntimeProbe struct {
	BehaviorStatement
	Vars   map[string]string
	Covers []Grant
}
    RuntimeProbe is a positive execution witness on a disposable fixture.
    Covers names the runtime privileges for which the application considers
    it evidence. Each probe runs as Role with Vars in a separate rolled-back
    savepoint.

type SQLBinding struct {
	Roles    []string
	Access   []PolicyAccess
	Variants []Statement
	Skip     bool
}
    SQLBinding assigns one inventoried site to its execution roles. Dynamic
    builders require reviewed named variants. Skip requires a registered
    exception.

type SQLInventory struct {
	Sites    []SQLSite
	Findings []string
}
    SQLInventory retains reviewed sites and reports unreviewed dynamic SQL and
    stale exceptions.

func CollectSQL(ctx context.Context, cfg InventoryConfig) (SQLInventory, error)
    CollectSQL resolves Go types and constants using the installed Go toolchain,
    including aliases and imported constants. Escaping method values are
    dynamic sites. Run it once per build configuration whose SQL belongs in the
    inventory.

func (inv SQLInventory) BindRoles(bindings map[string]SQLBinding) (RoleStatements, error)
    BindRoles produces a workload from the collected SQL. Missing and stale
    assignments, unreviewed dynamic sites and empty workloads fail validation.

type SQLMethod struct {
	Receiver, Method string
	Argument         int
}
    SQLMethod matches the package-qualified receiver type (without pointer or
    generic arguments). Argument is the zero-based SQL position in a method
    call.

type SQLSite struct {
	ID, File         string
	Line             int
	Receiver, Method string
	SQL              string `json:",omitempty"`
	Dynamic          bool   `json:",omitempty"`
	Exception        string `json:",omitempty"`
}
    SQLSite describes a static or dynamic call. ID is independent of line
    numbers.

type Statement struct {
	Name   string
	SQL    string
	Access []PolicyAccess `json:",omitempty"`
}
    Statement is application-owned SQL. Access supplies the complete relation
    and command list for complex statements when checking structural policy
    coverage.

```

## stdsql

```text
package stdsql // import "github.com/0xJean/tabula/stdsql"

Package stdsql provides ready-to-use database/sql transaction sessions,
scope/RLS plug-ins, savepoints, and read-only Direct pools for tabula.
It depends only on the Go standard library and github.com/0xJean/tabula.

FUNCTIONS

func SetLocalConfig(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, key, value string) error
    SetLocalConfig sets a PostgreSQL transaction-local GUC via set_config(...,
    true).

func SetLocalRole(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, role string) error
    SetLocalRole switches the PostgreSQL role for the duration of tx.


TYPES

type DirectPool[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    DirectPool owns a database/sql pool of read-only PostgreSQL connections.

func Direct[S any](driverName, postgresURL string, policy ScopePolicy[S]) (*DirectPool[S], error)
    Direct opens a dedicated read-only pool from a PostgreSQL URL and a
    registered database/sql driver (for example "postgres"). Call Session to
    bind each request and Close at shutdown. SetupTx requires a Runner.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Close() error
    Close releases the underlying connection pool.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Session(scope S) tabula.Session[S]
    Session binds the scope without opening a transaction or checking out a
    connection.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) SetConnMaxIdleTime(d time.Duration)
    SetConnMaxIdleTime sets the maximum amount of time a connection may be idle.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) SetConnMaxLifetime(d time.Duration)
    SetConnMaxLifetime sets the maximum amount of time a connection may be
    reused.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) SetMaxIdleConns(n int)
    SetMaxIdleConns sets the maximum number of idle connections in the pool.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) SetMaxOpenConns(n int)
    SetMaxOpenConns sets the maximum number of open connections to the database.

func (p *DirectPool[S]) Stats() sql.DBStats
    Stats returns database/sql pool statistics.

type Runner[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Runner opens scoped PostgreSQL transactions on a *sql.DB and binds them to
    Session[S] handles.

func NewRunner[S any](db *sql.DB, policy ScopePolicy[S]) *Runner[S]
    NewRunner creates a Runner backed by db and policy.

func (r *Runner[S]) Within(ctx context.Context, scope S, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    Within runs fn in a read-write transaction with the database default
    isolation.

func (r *Runner[S]) WithinIsolation(ctx context.Context, scope S, level sql.IsolationLevel, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    WithinIsolation runs fn in a transaction with the requested isolation level.

func (r *Runner[S]) WithinOptions(ctx context.Context, scope S, opts *sql.TxOptions, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) (err error)
    WithinOptions runs fn inside a transaction started with opts. SetupTx runs
    immediately after BeginTx. Errors and panics roll back automatically.

func (r *Runner[S]) WithinReadOnly(ctx context.Context, scope S, fn func(context.Context, *Session[S]) error) error
    WithinReadOnly runs fn in a READ ONLY transaction.

type ScopePolicy[S any] struct {
	// SetupTx runs once right after BeginTx inside the transaction (for example
	// calling SetLocalRole and SetLocalConfig for PostgreSQL RLS).
	SetupTx func(ctx context.Context, tx *sql.Tx, scope S) error
	// GuardQuery optionally inspects every SQL string before execution and
	// rejects forbidden statements (e.g. SET ROLE or set_config from adapters).
	GuardQuery func(query string) error
	// IsUnscoped reports whether scope represents an unscoped (cross-partition) call.
	IsUnscoped func(scope S) bool
}
    ScopePolicy plugs application-specific isolation rules (scope GUC variables,
    SET LOCAL ROLE, statement timeouts, or SQL guards) into a Runner and its
    Sessions without coupling tabula to any particular domain model.

func NoScopePolicy() ScopePolicy[struct{}]
    NoScopePolicy returns an empty ScopePolicy for applications that do not use
    row-level tenant scoping.

type Session[S any] struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Session implements tabula.Session[S] over one database/sql *sql.Tx.

func NewSession[S any](tx *sql.Tx, scope S, policy ScopePolicy[S]) *Session[S]
    NewSession wraps an existing *sql.Tx with scope and policy.

func (s Session) Each(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, decode func(func(...any) error) error) error
    Each streams all rows of query through decode.

func (s *Session[S]) Exec(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (int64, error)
    Exec executes a statement and returns its affected row count.

func (s *Session[S]) ReadOnly() bool
    ReadOnly reports whether this session was opened as a READ ONLY transaction.

func (s *Session[S]) Returning(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Returning executes a write with RETURNING and scans the returned row into
    dest.

func (s *Session[S]) Savepoint(ctx context.Context, name string, fn func(context.Context) error) (err error)
    Savepoint runs fn inside a PostgreSQL SAVEPOINT. On error or panic, changes
    made inside fn are rolled back to the savepoint while keeping the enclosing
    transaction usable; on success the savepoint is released.

func (s Session) Scan(ctx context.Context, query string, args []any, dest ...any) error
    Scan executes a single-row query and scans into dest.

func (s *Session[S]) Scope() S
    Scope returns the session's bound scope value.

func (s *Session[S]) Tx() *sql.Tx
    Tx returns the underlying *sql.Tx for low-level escape hatches.

func (s *Session[S]) Unscoped() bool
    Unscoped reports whether this session bypasses row-level scope predicates.

```

## CLI

```text
Usage: tabula <command> [flags]
  tabula check           Prepare and explain statements from a SQL snapshot.
  tabula check-rls       Check row-level security settings on tables.
  tabula inventory       Collect SQL call sites and their role assignments from Go source.
  tabula verify-roles    Prepare and explain each role's workload.
  tabula grants          Compare direct grants with a manifest and report reconciliation SQL.
  tabula minimize        Trial grant removals in a rolled-back transaction.
  tabula catalog         Snapshot the PostgreSQL authorization catalog or compare saved snapshots.
  tabula check-policies  Classify installed policies using application rules.
  tabula check-coverage  Check RLS command coverage for a role workload.
  tabula test-rls        Run a role and scope matrix against expected rows or denials.
Use tabula <command> -h for flags.
```

### tabula check

```text
Usage of check:
  -dsn string
        PostgreSQL DSN (defaults to TABULA_DSN)
  -role string
        optional PostgreSQL role to SET LOCAL ROLE before PREPARE/EXPLAIN
  -snapshot string
        path to a sqlcheck snapshot file
```

### tabula check-rls

```text
Usage of check-rls:
  -dsn string
        PostgreSQL DSN (defaults to TABULA_DSN)
  -forbid-roles string
        comma-separated role names forbidden from appearing directly in policies
  -force
        require FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (default true)
  -restrictive
        require at least one RESTRICTIVE policy per table
  -schema string
        PostgreSQL schema to audit (default "public")
  -tables string
        comma-separated table names that must have RLS enabled (default: all RLS tables in schema)
```

### tabula inventory

```text
Usage of inventory:
  -bindings string
        emit role workload using site assignments in this JSON file
  -config string
        path to command-specific JSON configuration
```
